class.name: RouteBindingResource
class.brief_description: One gamepad input routed to an action or a callback by [InputRouter].
class.description: A binding names one physical pad input (a button, half or all of an axis, or a stick), an optional [member gate] button that makes it a chord, a [member trigger] that decides when it fires, the response that shapes analog values, and what it drives: an [member action], a callback, the virtual pointer, or all of these. Attach it with [method InputRouter.attach], or list it in a [GamepadMap]. The router copies each placement from the compiled template in its route map ([GamepadBakedMaps]), keyed by [member id] and [member scheme]; a binding the map lacks is compiled into a new map at the next frame, with a warning to rebake. The first binding to claim an input owns it until the input is released. In the editor, the inspector shows a summary from [method describe], the input and gate as each pad family labels them, a [b]Listen[/b] button that sets the input from a connected pad (hold a button first to make it the gate), response presets, and a live preview that shapes the selected pad's input with the router's own functions. Properties the current [member source] and [member trigger] do not use are hidden but still saved. In editor builds, a placed binding whose properties change while the game runs is recompiled, and its rows retune from the next frame.

method.name: describe
method.description: Returns a one-line summary with generic labels, such as [code]"LB + RT (analog)"[/code] or [code]"X > Y > A (sequence)"[/code]. For logs and tools.

method.name: make_response_curve
method.description: Returns a new editable [Curve] for [param preset]: five points with matching tangents, from (0, 0) to (1, 1). Assign it to [member response].

members.member: An [InputMap] action this binding drives through [Input], so [method Input.is_action_pressed] and [method Node._input] see it. [constant TRIGGER_PRESS] and [constant TRIGGER_REPEAT] hold the action while the input is down, with the shaped value at the press as its strength, and [constant TRIGGER_REPEAT] presses it again on every repeat; [constant TRIGGER_ANALOG] follows the shaped value. [constant TRIGGER_RELEASE], [constant TRIGGER_HOLD], [constant TRIGGER_TAP] and [constant TRIGGER_SEQUENCE] press it for one frame each time they fire. Several bindings may drive one action: it stays pressed while any of them holds it, and letting go of one while another holds it sends no event. Empty: no action.
The output just past [member deadzone]. Raise it when the game applies a deadzone of its own downstream, so small movements still register.
The axis read when [member source] is [constant SOURCE_AXIS].

Which part of [member axis] is the input: [code]-1[/code] the negative half, [code]0[/code] the full axis from [code]-1[/code] to [code]1[/code], [code]1[/code] the positive half. Triggers only use the positive half. Each half is its own input slot, so one stick axis can carry two bindings.
The button read when [member source] is [constant SOURCE_BUTTON]. Buttons are positional: [constant JOY_BUTTON_A] is the bottom face button on every pad.
The context this binding goes into when [method InputRouter.attach] names none. Registered with the router on attach.
Raw magnitude below which the output is [code]0[/code]. Between [member deadzone] and [member saturation] the output rescales from [member anti_deadzone] to [code]1[/code].
How a stick's deadzone applies. See [enum DeadzoneShape].

A modifier button that must be held for this binding to fire, making it a chord such as [code]LB + A[/code]. While the gate is held its chords form a layer: they win over ungated bindings for the same input in any context on the path (see [GamepadContext]), and inputs the layer does not bind behave as without the gate, except that a stick the layer binds in any direction belongs to the layer whole. An input pressed shortly before its gate still counts, within [method InputRouter.get_chord_window]. A button used as a gate fires its own ungated binding on release only, and only if no chord used it; its unbound presses never pass to Godot. Pressing or releasing the gate changes what its inputs mean, so claims on them end: on press, the ungated claims on every input the layer covers (each button and trigger it binds, each stick it binds in any direction); on release, the gate's own chords. An analog or pointer claim stops (its value goes to zero), any other is canceled; neither reads as a release. Any of those inputs still off rest is then [i]engaged[/i]: all its input is eaten until it returns to rest, so a held input never fires a chord or lands on another binding mid-press. [constant JOY_BUTTON_INVALID]: no gate.
Seconds the input must stay pressed before [constant TRIGGER_HOLD] fires.

The binding's name: the key of its template in the route map, of player rebinds ([method InputRouter.set_override]) and of named callbacks ([method InputRouter.set_callback]). Required; the router refuses a binding without one. One id may have one binding per [member scheme].
A display name for prompts and tools. Baked with the template.
For a stick axis: if [code]true[/code], the input reads [code]0[/code] while the stick's other axis is pushed further, so diagonal movement drives only the dominant direction.

For a stick: if [code]true[/code], the shaped stick also moves the virtual pointer at [member pointer_speed]. Read it with [method InputRouter.take_pointer_delta] and [method InputRouter.get_pointer_velocity].
Virtual pointer speed in pixels per second at full deflection.
Shaped value at which an analog input counts as pressed.

Order among bindings for the same input in the same context, highest first, after gated bindings. Two bindings with the same input, gate, context and priority are a clash that [method InputRouter.check_maps] reports.
Shaped value below which a pressed analog input counts as released. Kept at or below [member press_threshold], so the gap between them is hysteresis.
Seconds from the press to the first [constant InputRouter.PHASE_REPEATED] for [constant TRIGGER_REPEAT].
Seconds between repeats after the first. A late frame fires one repeat, not a burst.

Maps the deadzoned magnitude, [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code], to the output. Sampled into a table when compiled; bindings with the same curve share one table. Editing the curve's points emits [signal Resource.changed]. Null: linear.
Raw magnitude at which the output reaches [code]1[/code].
The control scheme this binding belongs to. Empty: it applies under every scheme. Otherwise it applies only while [method InputRouter.set_scheme] selects this scheme.
For [constant TRIGGER_SEQUENCE]: up to four [enum JoyButton]s to press, in order, after the input.
The kind of physical input.
The stick read when [member source] is [constant SOURCE_STICK].
Longest press, in seconds, that [constant TRIGGER_TAP] counts as a tap.
When the binding fires, and which [enum InputRouter.Phase]s its callback receives.

constants.constant: An axis or half of one, [member axis] and [member axis_direction]. The callback value is a [float].
A whole stick, [member stick]. The callback value is a [Vector2].
[constant InputRouter.PHASE_PRESSED] when the input crosses [member press_threshold], [constant InputRouter.PHASE_RELEASED] when it falls below [member release_threshold].
[constant InputRouter.PHASE_HELD] once the input has been held for [member hold_time], then [constant InputRouter.PHASE_RELEASED].
[constant InputRouter.PHASE_TAPPED] on a release within [member tap_time] of the press. A longer press fires nothing.
[constant InputRouter.PHASE_PRESSED], then [constant InputRouter.PHASE_REPEATED] after [member repeat_delay] and every [member repeat_interval] while held. For menus.
[constant InputRouter.PHASE_CHANGED] on every change of the shaped value, including the return to zero.

[constant InputRouter.PHASE_PRESSED] when the input and then each button of [member sequence] are pressed in order within [method InputRouter.get_sequence_timeout]. A wrong button restarts it. Sequences watch presses without claiming them.
The deadzone applies to the stick's magnitude and keeps its direction.
The deadzone applies to each axis on its own, which snaps toward the axes.
Radial, then an axis under half the deadzone is zeroed, so straight pushes stay straight.
A gentle curve, [code]x^1.6[/code]: finer control near the center.
A steep curve, [code]x^2.5[/code]: much finer control near the center, for aiming.
